Jensen closed his GTC Berlin 2026 keynote with this Hermes Agent demo as the finale. 

He introduced it by saying the way to build an agent is to ask an agent to build it for you, so he installed and set up a customized Hermes in one prompt. 

Then he used Hermes, running on @nvidia RTX Spark, to create a simulated training environment for the @huggingface Microduck. Hermes planned an obstacle course with Nemotron and had GPT-6 Astra build it using FreeCAD, Omniverse libraries, Blender, Newton, and Isaac Lab. Hermes trained thousands of simulated ducks on that course until the validated policy was ready to run on the real robot in the physical world.

At Nous, we believe open source is a practical tool as much as a philosophical ideal. It gives users the ability to build powerful, complex workflows chaining numerous local+cloud models, devices, and tools themselves instead of waiting for a company to enable them.

Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

AI has made my research better. But I realized today it’s also costing me something...

When I was in middle school, I asked my grandpa what a word meant. He told me to go grab the dictionary and look it up. I asked why I couldn’t just look it up online. He said that would get me the answer for sure, but I’d be missing something. When you open a dictionary, you see all the words next to the one you’re looking up, and you end up learning a few of those too. Looking it up online gets you the one word and nothing around it. Metric might be the most important DEX launch of the year.
Here’s why:
Metric went live yesterday on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain. Before it had a frontend it already cleared ~$21.9B as an aggregator-only venue.
The problem it fixes:
• Classic AMMs discover price inside the pool. When the real market moves, the pool only catches up once an arber trades it back in line, and LPs pay for that gap on every move.
• That’s tolerable for long-tail tokens with no price anywhere else. It’s backwards for assets whose price is set elsewhere: NVDA on Nasdaq, ETH on centralised order books, stablecoins at their peg. For these, an on-chain pool should follow the market, not rediscover it.
• Solana solved this with propAMMs (HumidiFi, SolFi), pools that quote off an external price. They now do 15 to 27% of on-chain DEX volume. On EVM, Tessera and Native run the same model. All of them are closed tho: one market maker, one book.
What Metric is:
• An oracle-priced DEX. Price comes from Chainlink or Pyth, not from the pool’s token ratio. LPs fund bins at fixed % distances from that reference, and every bin moves with the oracle. No range management, no arb leakage on reference moves.
• No explicit fee: traders pay the spread, split between LPs, the curator and the protocol.
• Permissionless: a curator runs pricing, anyone can LP. That’s the gap between Metric and every propAMM before it.
Why it matters:
• Tokenized stocks are the cleanest use case for oracle pricing there is, and Metric is built for them. A Multiplier Oracle handles splits and dividends, Robinhood’s ERC-8056 natively. Already running the bStocks pairs on BNB Chain and stock pools on Robinhood Chain.
• A propAMM lives or dies on stale quotes, and that part is engineered: on Ethereum, quote updates land only in blocks with a trade, via builders covering ~97 to 98% of blocks. BSC has a protected lane. Robinhood Chain has neither, which makes it the real test.
• Guardrails sit in the contracts, not the UI: green pools need oracle-anchored pricing, a verified curator and an immutable StopLoss. Extensions can reject a trade, never change a price.
• CTO is ex-Uniswap senior eng manager, audited by Zellic and Sherlock.
Points and referrals are already wired into the app btw, so being early here looks worth it imo. An airdrop down the line wouldn’t surprise me.

Safe keeps the keys on your own Ledgers, but the transaction usually gets built in the Safe web app. Bybit lost $1.5B that way: the frontend got compromised and the signers approved what their screens showed them.

MPC adds a policy engine, limits, whitelists, second approvals. The vendor holds a key share and co-signs everything you do. Subscription, KYC, and if they pause you, you're paused.

Custodians go all the way: You own a claim, they own the keys. Works for an ETF. For a private person it mostly moves the subpoena to a different address.
